summary: Any board cell can affect the required final board, so a correct in-place transformation must inspect all mn cells in the worst case. Boundary flood fill plus finalization processes each cell only a constant number of times.

optimality.argument: Consider a board initially filled with X. If an algorithm leaves any cell unread, changing that cell to O changes the required final board: a boundary O must survive, while an interior singleton O must be captured after being recognized. Thus exact in-place transformation requires Omega(mn) cell inspections in the worst case. The current boundary scans, flood fill, and final pass perform constant total work per cell, giving O(mn) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: On an all-X board, changing any unseen cell to O changes the required processing or final value at that position, so arbitrary cells cannot be skipped.
Each cell is marked and enqueued at most once, and the final nested loop visits every cell once.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover an enclosed region, a boundary survivor, and the one-cell board; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
